The error comes from `prompt_lens` covering only the 128 math texts, not the 48 nonmath chats. For the chats I'll locate the same template position directly: take the three template token ids preceding text 0's answer (`<start_of_turn>`, `model`, newline) and find their first occurrence in each chat. The last prompt token is then the newline. The rest of the computation is unchanged: summary-vector statistics only.

Two small bugs, no new results. At layer 0 the difference is exactly zero, as it must be: every text has the same last prompt token (the newline after "model"), hence the same embedding. And the name `unit` was still bound to an old numeric variable, because the block that defined it never ran. I'll redefine the helper safely and start from layer 1; nothing else changes. The nonmath position check confirms the newline before each chat's first answer token, so both sets now sit at the same template position.

The pass-2 contrast is very stable: split-half cosine is 0.96–1.00 at layers 1–12. But it has almost no agreement with the same contrast built from gen_1 (cosine −0.19 to +0.20). For identical template positions that is impossible, so either gen_1's array is laid out differently (for example layers before problems) or its "last prompt token" is a different position.

There is also a confound. Every math prompt ends with the same fixed instruction ("Solve the problem step by step…####"), while the chats end freely. So at the last prompt token this direction mostly encodes the instruction suffix, not math content. Pass 4 already showed that suffix has no effect on gold solutions (≤ 0.02 nats).

Before deciding whether a content-matched contrast is worth a pass, I'll check H's shape and the cosine of the pass-2 math mean with gen_1's math mean, layer by layer. They should agree near 1.0 if the layouts match.

The array layout is fine (H is 512 × 19 × 640), and the overall means agree (cosine 0.94–0.99 from layer 4 on), but only because the massive channels dominate them. The non-massive part disagrees, and the norms differ by 30–40%. So gen_1's "last prompt token" is evidently a different template position from pass 2's newline. That doesn't matter much, because the pass-2 direction is confounded anyway: every math prompt shares the identical instruction suffix, so its very high split-half stability reflects that fixed text, not math content. Pass 4 already showed the suffix has no effect on gold solutions, so I'm closing the prompt-end abliteration line.
